title: The Trial Balance in Double Entry Accounting

blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how accountants ensure that all financial transactions are correctly recorded? The trial balance is a key tool in this process.

blocks.markdown: In accounting, the trial balance is a statement that lists all the balances from the ledger accounts. It is used to verify that the total debits equal the total credits in the ledger, ensuring that the accounting entries are mathematically correct.

blocks.title: Definition of Trial Balance
blocks.text: A trial balance is a bookkeeping worksheet in which the balances of all ledgers are compiled into debit and credit account columns.

blocks.markdown: To prepare a trial balance, you list all the ledger accounts and their balances, categorizing them into debits and credits. The sum of the debit balances should equal the sum of the credit balances.

blocks.title: Extracting a Trial Balance
blocks.prompt: Given the following ledger balances, prepare a trial balance.

steps.text: List all ledger accounts with their respective debit or credit balances.
Sum up the debit balances and the credit balances separately.
Ensure that the total debits equal the total credits.

blocks.answer: The trial balance is balanced if total debits equal total credits.

blocks.markdown: However, a trial balance will not reveal all types of errors. For instance, it cannot detect errors of omission, errors of commission, or compensating errors.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, if a trial balance does not balance, check for simple arithmetic errors, incorrect ledger balances, or transposition errors first.

points: A trial balance is used to verify the arithmetic accuracy of ledger entries.
It does not detect all types of errors, such as errors of omission or commission.
